title: Orthogonalization and sanity clauses for LLM A/B rollouts (working notes)
content:
Status: draft — collection of patterns and concrete clauses we want in every cross-functional LLM A/B or canary exposure. Purpose: reduce correlated failure modes across cohorts, make small experiments auditable, and enable safe blind A/B evaluation where product and model teams cannot leak signals that bias results.

Quick problem statement:
- We keep seeing subtle cross-cohort contamination (caches, shared feature flags, telemetry dedup) that biases A/B signals.
- Behavioral regressions slip because teams look at sampled outputs and re-train on visible failure modes before the metric signal stabilizes.
- Need a lightweight operational contract that sits between product, ML, infra, and SRE.

Core principles (short):
1) Orthogonalization: isolate experiment path from ancillary systems (caches, rerankers, personalization hooks).
2) Blindness: prevent premature human-driven model changes while primary metrics are still immature.
3) Sanity clauses: automatic, simple checks that can pause/kill exposure before downstream customers notice.
4) Low-friction onboarding: steward-run checklist so teams can self-serve safe experiments.

Minimum-viable orthogonalization checklist (for each experiment):
- Route: dedicated route id + header token to avoid generic routing heuristics.
- Cache isolation: use experiment-scoped KV prefix OR bypass prefix checks to prevent cross-population hits.
- Feature flags: freeze any shared personalization flags; record any exceptions in the runbook.
- Synthetic traffic: add deterministic synthetic probes that exercise edge behaviors and are flagged in telemetry.
- Side-effects: confirm no writes to shared user data or metrics collectors that could leak cohort identity.

Blind A/B protocol (operational):
- Pre-registration: experiment owner files short hypothesis + primary metric + minimum detectable effect (MDE) and target sample size (JIRA ticket).
- Steward assignment: a steward (non-owner) is assigned to enforce the blind window. Stewards are rotated weekly.
- Blind window: product/ML teams agree to no model weight/config changes and no manual output edits for at least 72 hours after 50% of MDE sample is collected.
- Stakeholder visibility: dashboards show metrics but hide cohort labels; raw examples accessible only to steward + SRE.

Sanity clauses (auto, must run at 1m, 5m, 15m cadence while experiment active):
- Crash rate > 0.5% above baseline -> immediate pause.
- Token latency p95 > baseline + 150ms for 5m -> scale down exposure and notify on-call.
- Unit cost per request > 2x expected for >10m -> revert to cost-fallback model.
- Toxicity/hallucination signals (from safety classifier) increase by >2x -> downgrade traffic to conservative model and trigger investigation.
- Response-length anomaly (avg tokens +/- 3 std) -> mark run for human review.

Signal orthogonality heuristics (to detect contamination):
- Cohort fingerprinting: compute per-cohort unique request hash rate; sudden increases indicate routing leaks.
- KV miss-rates: compare cache-hit ratios across cohorts; matching distributions when they should differ = contamination.
- Time-of-day skew: if one cohort mimics traffic pattern of another within 15 minutes, suspect replayed requests or shared proxies.
- Downstream feature parity: ensure downstream services receive identical headers except the experiment token.

Runbook snippets for stewards (templates):
- If any sanity clause triggers -> escalate to oncall SRE + steward slack channel and flip experiment to "paused".
- If metric drift observed but no auto-trigger -> steward to request sampling freeze and run offline list of 200 examples for blinded annotation.
- If contamination suspected -> steward issues a temporary tear-down and re-runs with stricter isolation flags.

Unresolved / TODOs (notes to self):
- Define exact classifier and thresholds for hallucination/toxicity signal (work with safety team).
- Add automated thermometers for cost-per-token by model config (Metric: cost/tok rolling 1h).
- Prototype cohort-fingerprint detector (Marcus + infra) and add as SaaS alert rule.
- Decide whether steward can unblind for limited emergency (legal/SOC) — require audit trail if allowed.

Ceremony & timeline suggestion for a simple AB (2-week cadence):
- Day -5: preregister and steward assignment; infra smoke test (isolation flags).
- Day -3: synthetic traffic + observability bake.
- Day 0: ramp to target slice (5% -> 25% over 24h) with manual checkpoint.
- Day 3: reach target traffic. Blind window active until Day 6 (or 50% MDE).
- Day 7–9: analysis window (steward-led, blinded annotations).
- Day 10–14: wrap, unblind, run post-hoc sanity checks, decision: promote, iterate, or rollback.

Notes on human factors:
- People will want to peek. Make it easy for stewards to surface succinct anonymized failure trends so curiosity is satisfied without breaking blindness.
- Keep gate thresholds conservative early; loosen thresholds as we learn.

Example short commit message for infra changes (useful for audit):
"experiment-route: add isolated kv-prefix and exp-header; disable global cache for JIRA-4218"

Quick links / references: see linked artifacts above.

If you're reading this and want to help: ping @marcus or add to JIRA-4218. I'll iterate this into a templated runbook and steward dashboard once we validate the cohort-fingerprint detector.
